why: Explain a scary notice; must not say 'ignore it'; holding reply draft

turns.user: I got a letter from a lawyer saying I owe Rs 80,000 to a finance company and must pay in 15 days or they will file a case. I never took any loan from them. What does this mean?
turns.reply: Hello! I am Haq, a legal first-aid assistant. Please note I am not a lawyer. A legal notice from a finance company for a loan you never took is serious and must not be ignored. Since this involves a legal notice and potential court case, you should consult a lawyer or use free legal aid (call the NALSA helpline at 15100). When did you receive the notice, and do you have any documents or messages from them?
turns.lawyerReason: This involves a formal legal notice threatening a case, which requires a lawyer's guidance or free legal aid.
nextActions: How to reply to the notice?

draft.title: Interim Holding Reply to Legal Notice
draft.document:
To,
[ADVOCATE'S NAME OR FINANCE COMPANY'S NAME],
[SENDER'S ADDRESS],

Subject: Interim reply to your legal notice dated [DATE OF NOTICE] regarding alleged dues of Rs 80,000.

Sir/Madam,

I, [YOUR FULL NAME], resident of [YOUR FULL ADDRESS], am in receipt of your legal notice dated [DATE OF NOTICE] sent on behalf of your client, [FINANCE COMPANY'S NAME]. 

I categorically deny any liability whatsoever regarding the alleged loan amount of Rs 80,000 mentioned in your notice. I have never availed of any such loan from your client. 

As your notice refers to a transaction of which I have no knowledge or record, please provide copies of the alleged loan agreement, account statements, and any supporting documents relied upon, so that I may examine the matter fully.

I am currently consulting my legal counsel to review the matter in detail. A substantive reply will be submitted upon receipt of the requested documents and completion of legal advice.

Yours faithfully,

[YOUR FULL NAME]
[YOUR PHONE NUMBER]
[YOUR EMAIL ADDRESS]
draft.howToSend: 1. Send this interim reply via Speed Post or Registered Post with Acknowledgement Due (RPAD) to the lawyer/company who sent the notice, and keep a copy for your records along with the postal receipt. 2. Keep the original notice and envelope safely. 3. Consult a lawyer or contact your District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) or call the NALSA helpline at 15100 before the 15-day deadline expires.
